sections.html:
Bullitt County is the Louisville suburb that grew into a distribution hub, just south of Jefferson County. Shepherdsville is the county seat, and Mount Washington is the largest city. Interstate 65 runs through the middle of the county, and warehouse and business parks cluster along it. About a fifth of the county, in the west, is Fort Knox training land, so not every acre is on the market.

The 2025 population is 86,454, up 5.1 percent since April 2020. The typical owner-occupied home is valued at $247,200, owners hold 84.9 percent of homes, and typical rent is $987. Builders took out 654 permits in 2025 against 34,722 housing units, so new construction is a real competitor for any seller. Typical owner cost is $1,561 a month with a mortgage and $524 without one.

sections.h2: Where to pay and who to call
sections.html:
The Sheriff's Office takes the money and distributes it to the state, county, schools and special districts. It sits on the first floor of the courthouse at 300 South Buckman Street in Shepherdsville, phone 502-543-2514. Mail goes to PO Box 205, Shepherdsville, KY 40165. From October 1 through December 31 you can also pay by check at any Stock Yards Bank branch in the county.

Assessments belong to the PVA, whose county annex is at 149 North Walnut Street, phone 502-543-7480. The County Clerk, at 502-955-6369, gives payoff figures for delinquent bills from earlier years.

The clerk delivers the bills to the sheriff at the end of September, and most owners see them in the first week of October. If yours has not come by mid-October, call for a duplicate. The 2026 bills carry four due dates, by receipt or postmark.

  • November 1: face value less a 2 percent discount.
  • December 31: face value.
  • January 31: face value plus a 5 percent penalty.
  • April 15: face value plus a 21 percent penalty.

After April 1, the sheriff no longer accepts personal or business checks. Pay with cash, a certified check, a money order or a card, and expect the processor to set the card fee. Partial payments are refused.

The sheriff publishes a rate chart for each jurisdiction. These real estate rates are in the cents-per-$100 form Kentucky uses.

2026 Bullitt County real estate rates
JurisdictionReal estate rate
State10.30
County8.7
Health2.4
Library4.9
School73.10
County Extension0.90
Shepherdsville10.10
Mount Washington Fire20.0

The first six lines add up to 100.30. The Nichols, Southeast and Zoneton fire districts are each 10.0, and a Plum Creek water line of 1.0 applies to real estate in its area. Shepherdsville's own tax comes combined with the county bill. Other incorporated places, including Mount Washington, Hillview, Hunters Hollow, Pioneer Village, Fox Chase, Lebanon Junction and Hebron Estates, bill their own city tax, so call the city. The tax district code on your bill tells you which lines apply.

Bullitt County Public Schools serves nearly the whole county and accounts for the largest line on the bill, 73.10. The schools on Fort Knox are run by the Department of Defense Education Activity instead, so a Fort Knox address is handled differently.

An owner who is 65 or older on January 1 and lives in the home can reduce the assessment by up to $49,100. Bring proof of age, such as a driver's license, to the PVA with the application, and do it before paying the bill. A totally disabled owner qualifies under the state rule as well. The application is due at the PVA by December 31 of the tax year.

Request a conference at the PVA once your notice arrives. The tax roll is open for inspection for thirteen days starting the first Monday in May, and a filing at the County Clerk is due the workday after the inspection period ends. The board of assessment appeals sits for as many as five days, starting 25 to 35 days after inspection closes. Bring comparable sales and photos, because the board decides on evidence and a case with none is denied.

A Bullitt bill is a stack of separate charges, and which ones you see depends on where the house sits. Everyone pays the state, county, health, library, school and extension lines. After that, the tax district code on the bill decides whether a city tax, a fire district or the Plum Creek water line applies to you.

If you live in Shepherdsville, the city's charge is folded into the sheriff's bill. If you live in Mount Washington or one of the other incorporated places, you will get a second bill from the city, and the city answers questions about it. A buyer's lender will want to see both paid, so a seller in a city should ask each office for a current balance.

sections.h2: Paying by check, at the bank or at the counter
sections.html:
The sheriff's office will take payment in person during its hours, and mail works if you use the Shepherdsville PO box. The bank option is handy for owners who live far from the courthouse: from October 1 through December 31, any Stock Yards Bank branch in the county takes check payments during business hours.

Plan around the April 1 cutoff. After that date, the sheriff accepts only cash, a certified check, a money order or a card, so a seller who waits for the last weeks of collection cannot write a personal check. Partial payments are turned away, which means the amount you send must cover the full bill.

sections.h2: Timing a sale around the tax calendar
sections.html:
Tax dates can help you pick a listing window. A house that closes before January 1 hands the next bill to the buyer, while one that closes in spring leaves the bill in your name, and the closing agent then splits the year. Neither route is a problem if the tax is current and the settlement statement spells out who pays.

If you have not paid yet, the November 1 date is the cheapest point of the whole year, and January 31 is where the penalty starts. A seller who knows a sale will close in the winter can pay in the discount window and keep the savings.

The bill goes to the January 1 owner, so a house that sells in the spring is still billed to the seller. The closing agent divides the year between the parties. The sheriff requires the full bill to be paid, so the settlement statement must show who pays.

  1. Call the sheriff at 502-543-2514 to confirm the current bill is paid.
  2. Ask the clerk at 502-955-6369 for a payoff on any earlier year.
  3. Check the PVA record and homestead status.
  4. Tell the closing agent who is paying the full bill.

Anything unpaid after April 15 moves to the clerk with a lien, and interest runs 1 percent a month, so ask for a payoff before the closing date. Sellers with inherited, tenant-occupied or heavily worn houses can often close with a cash buyer and have the tax paid from proceeds.

faqs.q: What is the Bullitt County sheriff's phone number for taxes?
faqs.a: Call 502-543-2514. The office is on the first floor of the courthouse at 300 South Buckman Street in Shepherdsville.

faqs.q: When does the Bullitt County 2% discount end?
faqs.a: For the 2026 bills it ends November 1, by receipt or postmark. December 31 is face value, January 31 adds 5 percent, and April 15 adds 21 percent.

faqs.q: Can I pay Bullitt County taxes at a bank?
faqs.a: Yes. Any Stock Yards Bank branch in the county takes check payments from October 1 to December 31 during business hours.

faqs.q: Does Shepherdsville charge a separate city tax?
faqs.a: No separate bill. Shepherdsville's tax is combined with the county bill, while other cities such as Mount Washington and Hillview bill their own city tax.

faqs.q: How much is the Bullitt County homestead exemption?
faqs.a: Up to $49,100 off the assessed value for owners 65 or older who live in the home on January 1. Apply at the PVA before paying the bill.
